movie_title: Which is better: Soap or hand sanitizer? - Alex Rosenthal and Pall Thordarson
introduction: Dig into the science of how soap breaks down a coronavirus, and the effectiveness of hand sanitizer

vocabulary.definition: molecules containing both hydrophilic (water-attracting) and hydrophobic (water-repelling) regions
vocabulary.example: The soap contains amphiphiles that help break down the virus's membrane.

vocabulary.definition: repelling water; tending to combine with or contain only non-aqueous solvents
vocabulary.example: The tails of the lipids are hydrophobic and repulsed by water.

vocabulary.definition: the protein shell of a virus particle, enclosing its genetic material
vocabulary.example: The capsid of the rhinoviruses makes it harder for soap to be effective.
Hand sanitizer has a destabilizing effect on the surface proteins of some viruses.
The chlorinated water kills harmful pathogens present on the hands.
It's crucial to follow the advice of accredited medical professionals during outbreaks.
